gloss: to take up a position; to claim a spot

definitions.gloss: to take up a position; to station oneself; to claim a spot
definitions.explanation: To settle into a particular location and occupy it, often implying staying there for some time. Originally a military term meaning to set up camp, now commonly used for everyday situations like claiming a seat or spot.

examples.japanese: {窓際|まどぎわ}に{陣取|じんど}った。
examples.english: I claimed a spot by the window.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもたちがテレビの{前|まえ}に{陣取|じんど}っている。
examples.english: The children have planted themselves in front of the TV.

examples.japanese: {花見|はなみ}の{場所|ばしょ}を{確保|かくほ}するために、{朝|あさ}から{公園|こうえん}に{陣取|じんど}っている{人|ひと}がいた。
examples.english: There were people who had been camped out in the park since morning to secure a spot for cherry blossom viewing.

notes:
A godan verb ({五段動詞|ごだんどうし}) conjugating with the る row. Originally a military term from {陣|じん} (battle formation/camp) + {取|と}る (to take), it has shifted to everyday use describing someone settling firmly into a spot.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {窓際|まどぎわ}に{陣取|じんど}る (claim a window seat)
- テレビの{前|まえ}に{陣取|じんど}る (plant oneself in front of the TV)
- {最前列|さいぜんれつ}に{陣取|じんど}る (take up a front-row position)

USAGE NOTES:
Implies staying put for a while, not just briefly sitting. Often carries a humorous or slightly exaggerated tone in everyday speech, as if the person is "occupying" a position like a soldier. The ている form is especially common, emphasizing the ongoing occupation of the spot.
